about: Shared acoustics table (owner C). Octave bands in Hz; every list has one value per band. Typical published values for North American light-frame houses, not measurements of this house: transmission loss from NRC Canada IR-761 (gypsum board walls) and IR-832-style glazing data, absorption from standard tables (Long, Architectural Acoustics; Egan, Architectural Acoustics). 63 Hz values are extrapolated.

exterior_brick_veneer_frame.label: brick veneer, 2x4 wood frame, batt insulation, 1/2 in. gypsum (about STC 55)

interior_stud_gypsum.label: 2x4 wood studs, one layer 1/2 in. gypsum each side, no insulation (about STC 34)

floor_ceiling_wood_joist.label: wood joists, plywood subfloor, 1/2 in. gypsum ceiling (about STC 38)

glazing_single.label: single pane 3 mm in a frame (about STC 26)

glazing_double.label: double pane 3-12-3 mm sealed unit (about STC 29)

glazing_triple.label: triple pane or laminated double unit (about STC 34)

door_interior_hollow.label: hollow-core interior door, closed, with undercut (about STC 18)

gypsum.label: painted gypsum board on studs (walls, ceilings)

furnishing_m2_per_floor_m2.about: Equivalent absorption of typical furnishings (sofas, beds, curtains, shelves) per m2 of floor, by room label. 'include_furniture=false' drops it.

sound_presets.about: Free-field level at 1 m (dBA) and spectrum shape (dB per band, unweighted, relative; scaled so the A-weighted sum equals level_dba). 'recording' is for the user's own clip: flat-ish shape, loudness picked by the user.
